findings.description: __aexit__ calls self.__exit__(None, None, None) instead of forwarding exc_type, exc_value and traceback, so the exception raised in the `async with` body is discarded.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the body of `async with attempt:` raises an exception. __exit__ gets None arguments, so it takes the success path, probably calling set_result(None). The failed attempt is recorded as a success and the exception is not recorded. __exit__ returns None, so the exception propagates, but retries never see the failure and the retry logic is bypassed. The sync __exit__ presumably does the exception handling when given the real exc_type, exc_value and traceback.
